neighbours.label: past-tense copula 'was' and the start of its predicate in narrative prose, against the present-tense or full-verb version of the same sentence
fire: Her main concern at the time was whether the bridge was safe.
The old mill was a landmark, and the owner was one of the richest men around.
Their mother was not happy, because the price was far too high.
In those days the harbor was a busy place and was full of ships.
The fact was that the manager wasn't ready.
My grandfather was a carpenter who was known across the county.
Its former director, whose background was medical, was not consulted.
The weather that summer was the worst anyone could recall.
quiet: Her main concern at the moment is whether the bridge is safe.
The old mill is a landmark, and the owner is one of the richest men around.
Their mother is not happy, because the price is far too high.
These days the harbor is a busy place and is full of ships.
The fact is that the manager isn't ready.
My grandfather built cabinets that sold across the county.
Its former director, whose background is medical, says little.
The weather that summer ruined the crops on every farm.

notes: Probes stayed below 0.2 of max (the max comes from long contexts), so this will probably miss the median-fire threshold. The - pole's direction promotes was/were/had, and the + pole fires on past full verbs and promotes 'recently'.
